subject: Advance commitment incentive discussion — CloudAtlas (2/3yr options)
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@cloudatlas.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudatlas.com, Anita Rao <anita@cloudatlas.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [CloudAtlas] Advance commitment proposal / three-year preference

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the observability hooks. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and are interested in an advance commitment to get predictable unit costs. High-level ask: we're evaluating a 3-year advance commitment but would also consider a 2-year if the economics are comparable.

Our initial target is roughly $1.2M committed consumption over three years (annualized target: ~$300k / $450k / $450k to align with product ramp). We are seeking a single consolidated discount on list rates in exchange for prepaying annually. Our procurement team has asked whether Redwood can offer a 28–32% effective discount for a 3-year prepay (or ~20–24% for 2-year). They're also asking for a shortfall protection / true-up mechanism and a billing schedule that mirrors our fiscal planning.

Attached is a starting SOW and a spreadsheet with rough usage profiles. Can you confirm what flexibility Redwood has on:
- 3-year vs 2-year blended discounts
- ramp breakpoints and conditional credits (for under-utilization)
- billing cadence for annual prepayments vs quarterly invoicing

We'd love a proposal we can take to procurement this week.

Best,
Maya
CloudAtlas Inc.

Attachments: CloudAtlas_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW), usage_profile.csv (referenced)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@cloudatlas.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [CloudAtlas] Advance commitment proposal / three-year preference

Maya — great to hear, and glad the demo was useful.

Quick reply with an operational proposal so you have something concrete to discuss with procurement:

Option A — 3-year annual prepay (preferred for unit economics)
• Total committed: $1.2M over 3 years (Year 1: $300k / Year 2: $450k / Year 3: $450k)
• Effective list discount: 26% applied to list token/embedding rates at invoice time
• Shortfall protection: 60% protection on Year 1 (if usage < 60% of committed, refundable credit up to 10% of Year-1 invoice), full true-up at contract anniversary
• Billing: annual invoice per year, due net 30; option to split into two equal invoices for Year 1 only
• Performance credit: up to 8% of annual invoice held and earned back based on usage thresholds in Year 2/3

Option B — 2-year annual prepay
• Total committed: $900k over 2 years (Year 1: $300k / Year 2: $600k)
• Effective discount: 20%
• Shortfall protection: 50% protection on Year 1, true-up at anniversary

Notes: these proposals are starting points — I'll loop in finance and legal for final approval on the discount limits and the credit mechanics. If procurement can confirm whether they prefer rigid annual prepay vs a phased billing schedule, that will help us firm up cashflow and discounting.

I've attached an internal pricing sketch. Karthik — can you weigh in on whether we should offer a 28% concession for a strategic logo (CloudAtlas is asking at the top end)?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Attachments: pricing_breakdown.xlsx

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: [CloudAtlas] Advance commitment proposal / three-year preference — internal ask for discount approval

Laura / Evelyn — forwarding CloudAtlas's ask and my suggested starting positions. TL;DR: CloudAtlas wants ~28–32% for a 3-year prepay; I'm proposing we offer 26% with an 8% holdback tied to usage (refundable credits at annual true-up). If we need to be more aggressive for logo/market signal we could move to 28% but that requires finance signoff on the holdback/accounting treatment.

Proposed commercial terms to approve:
• Commitment: $1.2M over 3 years (300 / 450 / 450) — annual prepayments preferred.
• Discount cap: approve up to 26% net for 3-year; allow escalation to 28% only with CFO ok.
• Holdback: 8% of each annual invoice held as a conditional credit; returned at anniversary if usage targets are met (usage targets are in the attached pricing_breakdown.xlsx).
• Shortfall mechanics: Year 1 protection at 60%, Year 2/3 true-ups only (no refunds beyond credits).
• Billing cadence: Net-30 annual invoice; acceptable to split Y1 into two invoices if procurement needs it.

Rationale: keeps unit economics within our modeled IRR while giving procurement meaningful downside protection. Also preserves the ability to offer a stretch concession for strategic wins.

Evelyn — what is the accounting/recognition impact of the 8% holdback? Will this require revenue deferral? If yes, any upper limit we should avoid hitting for multi-year deals this quarter?

Karthik — if we move to 28% to close, confirm whether you need an extra sales credit/comp exception.

Thanks — I'm asking for a one-day turnaround since procurement wants a term sheet this week.

— Stephanie

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: [CloudAtlas] Advance commitment proposal / three-year preference — internal ask for discount approval

Thanks for the clear summary. Approved with conditions.

Decision:
• Approve up to 26% effective discount on the three-year annual prepay outlined (1.2M total, 300/450/450).
• We will not automatically move to 28% — 28% needs CFO (Tom) sign-off and a brief note from Sales explaining strategic upsides (co-marketing, reference, marketplace listing).
• Approve the 8% holdback construct but cap aggregate deferred/held credits at $75k across this contract so our revenue recognition exposure is limited this quarter.
• Shortfall mechanics accepted as proposed (60% Year-1 protection).

Next steps for execution:
1) Stephanie: send the revised term sheet to Maya with the approved commercials and the DocuSign link (use the HubSpot deal above). Call out the $75k cap on held credits and the need for signature within 10 business days.
2) Karthik: prepare a short one-pager on the strategic rationale if procurement pushes for 28% (co-marketing, expected reference cadence, estimated ARR expansion).
3) Evelyn: confirm with accounting the revenue deferral language for the term sheet and whether the $75k cap requires any additional disclosure.

Once signed, we can convert the term sheet to SOW and route to legal — keep me posted.

— Laura
VP, Sales Operations
laura@redwood.com
